5770.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kléwos (whence Mycenaean Greek 𐀐𐀩𐀺 (ke-re-wo)), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱléwos.

5784.t: From the old oblique stem, *κραν- (*krān-), of κάρη (kắrē, “Homeric form of κάρα (kắrā, “the head”)”) + -ιον (-ĭon, diminutive suffix).

5779.t: From the o-grade κοντ- (kont-) of the root κεντ- (kent-) underlying κεντέω (kentéō, “prick”), κέντρον (kéntron, “centre”). The suffix is -ός (-ós, deverbal adjective and noun suffix).

5763.t: From κηδεύω (kēdeúō, “to care for”) + -εία (-eíā). The sense of "care for the dead" > "funeral" developed in the Hellenistic Koine era.

5780.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ḱorh₂- (“crow, raven”), apparently of imitative origin and with similar formations across multiple Indo-European branches; see Latin cornīx (“crow”) for more.

5794.t: Probably onomatopoeic. Compare βόμβος (bómbos, “humming, buzzing”), κόναβος (kónabos, “din, clash”) and κόμβα (kómba, “shearwater”).

5792.t: Unclear. The comparison with Latin curvus (“curved”) presupposes that the Greek adjective continues a reduced grade *kʷr-to-s with u coloring, which is phonetically difficult and places the comparison in doubt.

5785.t: Traditionally considered an old verbal noun from κρεμάννυμι (kremánnumi, “to hang”), however Beekes finds this impossible and leaves the etymology unexplained.

5799.t: From καρπός (kărpós, “fruit”) + -ιμος (-ĭmos, suffix for adjective of capability).

5755.t: From κατα- (kătă-, “against”) + the root of ἀγορεύω (ăgoreúō, “to speak”).

5746.t: From κατά (katá, “under, down”) + χράομαι (khrắomai, “to use, make use of, take part in, manage, administer”).

5798.t: Beekes finds improbable a derivation from κάπη (kápē, “crib, manger”). Probably related to Latin caupō (“innkeeper”); as the Greek could be from Pre-Greek, this would render the Latin a substrate borrowing, as well.

5765.t: The formation is like κνημίς (knēmī́s, “greave”). A comparable meaning can be found in Latin calidus (“with a bless on the head”).

5729.t: From κατα- (kătă-, denoting motion downwards) + λέγω (légō, “to choose, to say”).
